message.content:
In this repository, search the backend code (server-side code, not frontend/web UI code) for all distinct declarations of a method/function named "Close" (e.g. `func (x *Type) Close()` in Go, or `Close()` methods in other backend languages used here). 

Tasks:
1. First identify what language(s) the backend is written in (check root dirs, go.mod, package.json workspaces, etc.) to scope "backend" vs frontend/web.
2. Find every distinct declaration of a method named exactly `Close` across backend source files (exclude test files, i.e. files ending in _test.go or similar, from the declaration count only if the declaration itself is only in test files — but note if any declarations exist solely in test files).
3. For each declared `Close` method (grouped by receiver type), search for all call sites of `.Close()` on values of that type, and determine which ones are called from non-test server code (exclude _test.go files and any test/mock helper files). List the actual caller file:line for each.
4. Report: total distinct count of Close method declarations, and for each type whose Close is invoked by non-test code, list the caller file paths (with line numbers where possible).

Be thorough - use grep/ripgrep across the whole repo for "func.*Close(" and similar patterns, then verify by reading surrounding context to confirm receiver types. Report back concisely with file:line citations.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Confirmed: this is a single-language Go backend (module `github.com/usememos/memos`), with `web/` being the separate frontend (React/TS) SPA — excluded per task scope. Backend directories are `cmd`, `internal`, `server`, `store`, `proto` (generated gRPC gateway code).

## Summary

### 1. Language
Backend is **Go** (`go.mod` at repo root, module `github.com/usememos/memos`). Backend dirs: `cmd/`, `internal/`, `server/`, `store/`, `proto/`. `web/` is the frontend (npm/React) and was excluded.

### 2. Distinct `Close` declarations found

**Concrete method implementations (6 total, all in non-test files):**
| # | Receiver | Location |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `func (h *SSEHub) Close()` | `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:99` |
| 2 | `func (s *Store) Close() error` | `store/store.go:72` |
| 3 | `func (c *Cache) Close() error` | `store/cache/cache.go:187` |
| 4 | `func (d *DB) Close() error` (sqlite) | `store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:67` |
| 5 | `func (d *DB) Close() error` (postgres) | `store/db/postgres/postgres.go:46` |
| 6 | `func (d *DB) Close() error` (mysql) | `store/db/mysql/mysql.go:47` |

**Interface method signatures (contracts, not implementations) — 2:**
- `Close() error` in `Driver` interface — `store/driver.go:12` (implemented by items 4–6 above)
- `Close() error` in cache `Interface` interface — `store/cache/cache.go:31` (implemented by item 3)

**Declarations that exist only in test files (noted separately, not counted in the 6 above):**
- `func (tc *MemoFilterTestContext) Close()` — `store/test/filter_helpers_test.go:200`
- `func (tc *AttachmentFilterTestContext) Close()` — `store/test/filter_helpers_test.go:282`

So: **6 distinct non-test `Close` method declarations** (plus 2 interface contracts they satisfy, plus 2 test-only declarations).

### 3 & 4. Call sites from non-test server code

**`SSEHub.Close()`**
- `server/server.go:206` — `s.sseHub.Close()` (inside `Server.closeLongLivedConnections`, called from `Server.Shutdown`)
- (Other call sites are test-only: `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub_test.go:55-56`, `server/router/api/v1/test/sse_handler_test.go:120`)

**`Store.Close()`**
- `server/server.go:146` — `s.Store.Close()` (inside `Server.Shutdown`)
- (Other call sites are test-only: `store/demo_seed_test.go:28`, `store/deployment_config_test.go:421`, `store/test/*_test.go`, `server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:66`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go:438`, `server/router/rss/rss_test.go:22`, `server/router/api/v1/test/memo_service_benchmark_test.go:80`)

**`Cache.Close()`**
- `store/store.go:74` — `s.instanceSettingCache.Close()`
- `store/store.go:75` — `s.userCache.Close()`
- `store/store.go:76` — `s.userSettingCache.Close()`
  (all three inside `Store.Close()` itself, which is in turn invoked by `server/server.go:146` — a non-test caller chain)
- (Other call sites are test-only: `store/cache/cache_test.go:17,66,116,183`)

**`DB.Close()` (sqlite/postgres/mysql) / `Driver.Close()` interface**
- `store/store.go:78` — `return s.driver.Close()` (inside `Store.Close()`, dispatches polymorphically to whichever `*sqlite.DB`/`*postgres.DB`/`*mysql.DB` is active)
- No other non-test call sites found; all other `db.Close()` / `ts.Close()` calls involving DB driver instances are confined to `store/test/*_test.go`, `store/db/postgres/user_setting_test.go`, `store/test/migrator_test.go`, `store/test/migrator_upgrade_test.go`, or `store/test/containers.go` (a test-helper file).
- Note: inside each driver's own `Close()` implementation there's `return d.db.Close()` (e.g. `store/db/mysql/mysql.go:48`), but that closes the embedded standard-library `*sql.DB`, not a recursive call to the declared `DB.Close()`.

**Not relevant (false positives from the raw `.Close()` grep, not calls on our declared types):** `rows.Close()` (`sql.Rows`) throughout `store/db/*/**.go`, `response.Body.Close()`/`resp.Body.Close()` (`internal/httpgetter`, `internal/idp/oauth2`, `internal/webhook`, `internal/storage/s3`), `conn.Close()` in generated gRPC-gateway code (`proto/gen/api/v1/*.pb.gw.go`), `file.Close()`/`reader.Close()`/`output.Close()` in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` and `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service_storage.go` (standard `io.ReadCloser`/`os.File`), `listener.Close()`/`s.httpServer.Close()` in `server/server.go` (net.Listener / http.Server), and `writer.Close()`/`conn.Close()` in `internal/email/client.go`.

**Bottom line:** of the 6 distinct backend `Close` implementations, all 4 underlying types (`SSEHub`, `Store`, `Cache`, and the `DB`/`Driver` family) are exercised by non-test code, and every one of those call chains ultimately traces back to `server/server.go`'s `Server.Shutdown` method (lines 146 and 206), plus the internal cascade inside `store/store.go`'s own `Store.Close()` (lines 74-78).
